To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in situ biosensors based on the principle of mediated electron transfer are promising for bioprocess control.
in situ sensors are suitable for continuous monitoring of bioprocesses, whereas FIA is a useful technique for off-line monitoring.
the glucose electrode is suitable for on-line monitoring of glucose in animal cell cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new sensor systems for bioprocess control.
the development of biosensors for bioprocess control.
the development and optimisation of different biosensor devices for bioprocess control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FIA system with immobilised enzymes in a membrane is a suitable tool for bioprocess on-line monitoring of substrates, products and nutrients.
in situ sensors can be applied for the on-line monitoring of bioprocesses if the sensor system fulfils a number of requirements.
the FIA systems are superior to the in situ glucose electrode in terms of analytical ranges and sensitivites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biosensors are very useful devices for bioprocess control.
the biosensor systems described in this thesis are well suited for the determination of the substrates, inhibitors and nutrients of interest.
the biosensor systems developed are suitable for on-line bioprocess monitoring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosensor systems are suitable for bioprocessing.
the FIA systems can be used for bioprocess control and monitoring.
the in situ sensor can be used to monitor glucose in the bioreactor, but that the FIA systems are more suitable for off-line determination of the substrates in samples taken from the process.
